sample.source: Hash-verified public Open Food Facts label photos already in the local development benchmark
sample.split: 5 previously used development photos; this is not held-out or population-level evaluation.

reconstruction: Each source photograph was prepared in browser Canvas using the production 3,000 px long-edge cap and JPEG quality 0.98. SDK polygons were grouped into production-shaped OCR observations with per-token text, confidence, bounding boxes, reading order, image IDs, and a capture record, then passed to the production parser. For a panel with one explicit multi-basis header, label-like rows to the left of the value columns, complete values in each column, and unambiguous geometry, the parser aligns the independent top-to-bottom row orders and emits tentative candidates only for supported nutrient labels. It retains raw OCR lines and links each candidate to its source boxes. Per-field stage flags include these candidates; region precision/recall and independent column annotations remain unavailable.
networkPolicy: Images were supplied from the local process to Chrome memory; only GET requests to Paddle model hosting were allowed. The harness records no image/text payloads and blocks no local research data outside the process.
limitations: Only 5 convenience-sample photos (37 fields); all were previously used during OCR exploration, so no held-out score is claimed.

PP-OCRv5 is tested with its English model; PP-OCRv6 language is selected from existing human photo annotations only for this offline comparison. Production language detection and routing are not demonstrated.
OCR output strings are processed in memory for parsing and scoring but are not persisted.
Recognized box presence and confidence do not establish correct table row/column association; independent region and column annotations remain unavailable.
JavaScript heap metrics exclude WebAssembly linear memory, browser native allocations, and potential GPU memory.
No image bytes leave the local process; only GET requests to Paddle model hosting are made. This is a comparative development experiment, not held-out or population-level evidence.
